spawn_spec.prompt:
TASK: Build the frontend single-page app (vanilla JS + CSS, no framework, no build step) for the family-tree product.
DELIVERABLE: web/index.html, web/app.js, web/style.css. Hash-router SPA with routes: #/login (combined login/signup forms), #/trees (list of my trees), #/tree/<id> (the tree view).
SCOPE: /home/srijan/Documents/projects/dbms. Write ONLY web/**. The API server and all src/** files are OUT of scope (another node builds them); code against the contract below.
CONTEXT: REPO: /home/srijan/Documents/projects/dbms
Stack facts: Hono ^4.6 app on Cloudflare Workers (src/index.ts is the entry, export default app). TypeScript strict mode (pnpm typecheck = tsc --noEmit).
wrangler.jsonc already defines D1 binding named DB (database_name "dbms") and vars B2_ENDPOINT=https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com , B2_BUCKET=dbms-family-photos. .dev.vars has SESSION_SECRET.
Tests run with vitest. D1 is SQLite, so schema tests use better-sqlite3 (installed by another node). NEVER use Cloudflare KV anywhere.
DO NOT run any git commit - the lead commits. Stay strictly inside your write scope.
API CONTRACT (authoritative, do not redesign):
POST /api/signup {email,name,password,lang} -> 201 {user_id,email,name,lang}; 409 duplicate email.
POST /api/login {email,password} -> 200 {user} + Set-Cookie sid=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=604800. Wrong password -> 401.
POST /api/logout -> 204 clearing cookie. GET /api/me -> 200 current user or 401.
GET /api/trees -> 200 {trees:[{tree_id,name,role}]}. POST /api/trees {name} -> 201 {tree_id,name}; creator row auto-inserted into tree_access.
POST /api/trees/:id/access {email,role} -> 201, creator-only; unknown email -> 404; invalid role -> 400.
GET /api/trees/:id/generations -> 200 {generations:[{gen,couples:[{couple_id,other_info,child_count,partners:[{person_id,name,gender,dob,dod},...]}}]} ordered by gen asc (any member role).
GET /api/persons/:id -> 200 full person record (members only). POST /api/trees/:id/persons -> 201 {person_id} (editor+). PUT /api/trees/:id/persons/:pid -> 200 (editor+, partial update, whitelisted fields). DELETE /api/trees/:id/persons/:pid -> 200 (editor+; also delete dependent child_of rows and null couple partner references).
POST /api/trees/:id/couples {partner_a?,partner_b?,other_info?} -> 201 {couple_id} (editor+). POST /api/trees/:id/couples/:cid/children {person fields} -> 201 {person_id} creating the person AND a child_of row (editor+).
DELETE /api/trees/:id -> 200 creator-only; cascades child_of, couple, person, tree_access, trees in that order.
GET /api/kinship?tree=:tid&from=:pid&to=:pid -> 200 {from,to,relation_key,path,gloss,terms:{en,hi,ta,bn}}; no relation found -> 404 {error:"no_relation"}. Members only.
POST /api/persons/:pid/photo multipart form field "file" -> 201 {photo_url} (editor+); when B2 creds missing -> 503 {error:"b2_not_configured"}.
Static assets: everything not under /api/* is served from web/ via the ASSETS binding.
Errors are JSON {error:string}. 401 unauthenticated, 403 wrong role, 404 missing resource. Role hierarchy viewer < editor < creator; trees.created_by counts as creator even without a tree_access row.
Auth internals: password hashing PBKDF2-SHA256, 100000 iterations, 16-byte random salt, stored as pbkdf2$100000$salt_hex$hash_hex (WebCrypto crypto.subtle). Session cookie: payload {"uid","exp"} JSON, base64url, plus "." + base64url(HMAC-SHA256(payload, env.SESSION_SECRET)). Stateless, no KV.
PRODUCT FLOW (the professor's verbatim requirement, implement EXACTLY): the tree page renders the hierarchy of COUPLE nodes as connected boxes, one horizontal band per generation (generation 1 on top). Clicking a couple box opens a SMALL RECTANGULAR BOX showing: Father name, Mother name, and Other information (short snippet). Clicking the father name or mother name INSIDE that small box opens the BIG BOX: a modal with ALL details of that person - name, gender, date of birth, date of death, height, weight, address, mail, phone, job, degree, place, other information, photo (show uploaded photo if photo_url set), fetched via GET /api/persons/<pid>. The big modal also shows a KINSHIP BADGE: call GET /api/kinship?tree=<treeId>&from=<my person_id from GET /api/me>&to=<clicked pid>; display terms[userLang].term prominently with gloss underneath (e.g. "chacha - father's younger brother"); hide the badge gracefully if /api/me has no person_id or the call 404s.
Implementation requirements: fetch-based API client wrapping credentials (cookies are HttpOnly, same-origin, so plain fetch works); login stores nothing client-side besides in-memory state; after login navigate to #/trees; tree view fetches GET /api/trees/<id>/generations and lays out bands with SVG connector lines from each couple card bottom-center to the midpoint of its children's cards (derive parent-child links from the generations payload: a couple is a child-band member if its partners appear as children of the upper couple - the API returns bands in order, connect each couple in band n to the couple in band n-1 whose child_count covers it; simplest robust approach: draw connectors between consecutive bands from each upper card to each lower card horizontally nearest, acceptable for v1). Show role from GET /api/trees; if role is editor or creator show an "Add person" button opening a simple form calling POST /api/trees/<id>/persons (nice-to-have, must not block read flow). Error banners for failed requests; loading states; responsive to 360px width.
Design direction: warm paper background (#faf6ef), deep forest-green primary (#1f4d3a) with terracotta-red accent (#c0392b), serif display headings (Georgia stack), rounded-xl cards with soft shadows, generous whitespace, smooth 160ms hover transitions. Names rendered in the tree: partner_a name on the left, partner_b on the right, small heart or dot separator.
VERIFY: run node --check web/app.js (exit 0) and confirm web/index.html references only files that exist in web/. Also run pnpm typecheck from repo root to ensure you broke nothing outside web/ (it should still pass; web/ is plain JS excluded from tsc).
STOP WHEN: node --check passes, assets resolve, and every screen/route described above exists in the delivered files.

## YOU ARE A VISUAL ENGINEER. FOLLOW THIS WORKFLOW OR YOUR OUTPUT IS REJECTED.

**YOUR FAILURE MODE**: You skip design system analysis and jump straight to writing components with hardcoded colors, arbitrary spacing, and ad-hoc font sizes. The result is INCONSISTENT GARBAGE that looks like 5 different people built it. THIS STOPS NOW.

**EVERY visual task follows this EXACT workflow. VIOLATION = BROKEN OUTPUT.**

### PHASE 1: ANALYZE THE DESIGN SYSTEM (MANDATORY FIRST ACTION)

**BEFORE writing a SINGLE line of CSS, HTML, JSX, Svelte, or component code - you MUST:**

1. **SEARCH for the design system.** Use Grep, Glob, Read - actually LOOK:
   - Design tokens: colors, spacing, typography, shadows, border-radii
   - Theme files: CSS variables, Tailwind config, `theme.ts`, styled-components theme, design tokens file
   - Shared/base components: Button, Card, Input, Layout primitives
   - Existing UI patterns: How are pages structured? What spacing grid? What color usage?

2. **READ at minimum 5-10 existing UI components.** Understand:
   - Naming conventions (BEM? Atomic? Utility-first? Component-scoped?)
   - Spacing system (4px grid? 8px? Tailwind scale? CSS variables?)
   - Color usage (semantic tokens? Direct hex? Theme references?)
   - Typography scale (heading levels, body, caption - how many? What font stack?)
   - Component composition patterns (slots? children? compound components?)

**DO NOT proceed to Phase 2 until you can answer ALL of these. If you cannot, you have not explored enough. EXPLORE MORE.**

### PHASE 2: NO DESIGN SYSTEM? BUILD ONE. NOW.

If Phase 1 reveals NO coherent design system (or scattered, inconsistent patterns):

1. **STOP. Do NOT build the requested UI yet.**
2. **Extract what exists** - even inconsistent patterns have salvageable decisions.
3. **Create a minimal design system FIRST:**
   - Color palette: primary, secondary, neutral, semantic (success/warning/error/info)
   - Typography scale: heading levels (h1-h4 minimum), body, small, caption
   - Spacing scale: consistent increments (4px or 8px base)
   - Border radii, shadows, transitions - systematic, not random
   - Component primitives: the reusable building blocks
4. **Commit/save the design system, THEN proceed to Phase 3.**

A design system is NOT optional overhead. It is the FOUNDATION. Building UI without one is like building a house on sand. It WILL collapse into inconsistency.

### PHASE 3: BUILD WITH THE SYSTEM. NEVER AROUND IT.

**NOW and ONLY NOW** - implement the requested visual work:

| Element | CORRECT | WRONG (WILL BE REJECTED) |
|---------|---------|--------------------------|
| Color | Design token / CSS variable | Hardcoded `#3b82f6`, `rgb(59,130,246)` |
| Spacing | System value (`space-4`, `gap-md`, `var(--spacing-4)`) | Arbitrary `margin: 13px`, `padding: 7px` |
| Typography | Scale value (`text-lg`, `heading-2`, token) | Ad-hoc `font-size: 17px` |
| Component | Extend/compose from existing primitives | One-off div soup with inline styles |
| Border radius | System token | Random `border-radius: 6px` |

**IF the design requires something OUTSIDE the current system:**
- **Extend the system FIRST** - add the new token/primitive
- **THEN use the new token** in your component
- **NEVER one-off override.** That is how design systems die.

### PHASE 4: VERIFY BEFORE CLAIMING DONE

BEFORE reporting visual work as complete, answer these:

- [ ] Does EVERY color reference a design token or CSS variable?
- [ ] Does EVERY spacing use the system scale?
- [ ] Does EVERY component follow the existing composition pattern?
- [ ] Would a designer see CONSISTENCY across old and new components?
- [ ] Are there ZERO hardcoded magic numbers for visual properties?

**If ANY answer is NO - FIX IT. You are NOT done.**
